title: Kadamba Empire
capsule: The Kadambas were the first indigenous dynasty to rule the western Deccan and coastal Karnataka, founded by Mayurasharma around 345 CE after he defeated Pallava and other forces and established a capital at Banavasi. At their apex under Kakusthavarma (c. 435–455), the Kadambas extended authority across much of Karnataka and forged matrimonial alliances with the Guptas, Vakatakas, and Gangas, marking their peak diplomatic prestige. The dynasty was known for patronage of Sanskrit and Kannada literary culture and early Brahmanical temples in the western Deccan. The main Kadamba line ended in the mid-sixth century as Chalukya power under Pulakesi I absorbed their territory by around 540–550 CE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Kadambas are documented through copper-plate grants and inscriptions in Sanskrit and Kannada, but territorial extent is inferred from grant findspots and is approximate, particularly for outlying regions.
